newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks slump, NAPM deflates bonds.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks slump, NAPM deflates bonds.

text.p: Wall Street fell after a higher opening on Monday, hurt after stronger-than-expected purchasing managers data caused the bond market to skid.

The Dow industrial average was trading off about 30 points at 7301 after rising to an intraday high of 7354. The benchmark 30-year Treasury, which had a strong session start, was off 11/32 at a 6.94 percent yield.
The Nasdaq composite also retreated from a higher open, trading off five points at 1395.
The National Association of Purchasing Managers Index was 57.1 in May compared with a forecast 53.9 and 54.2 in April.
